nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Statistical Inference I
learning_outcomes: identify descriptive statistics and methods of data presentation
understand measures of central tendency and dispersion
understand probability and probability distributions
perform hypothesis testing; and
apply statistical inference techniques
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Introduction to statistics. Data collection and presentation. Measures of central tendency. Measures of dispersion. understand sampling distributions
apply non-parametric tests
understand time series analysis; and
apply regression analysis to real problems

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Introduction to Actuarial Science
learning_outcomes: describe what actuarial science is and career opportunities
understand the role of actuaries in various industries
apply basic financial mathematics concepts
understand principles of probability in actuarial problems; and
describe the development and history of actuarial science
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Introduction to actuarial science and the actuarial profession. Career paths for actuaries: insurance; pensions; investment; banking; consulting. Role of the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries (IFoA) and Society of Actuaries (SOA). Historical development of actuarial science. Basic concepts: compound interest; annuities; present values. Introduction to life tables. Overview of key actuarial models

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Differential Calculus for Act. Sci.
learning_outcomes: apply differentiation techniques to actuarial problems
solve optimization problems
apply calculus to financial mathematics
understand Taylor series and their applications; and
apply numerical methods
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Differentiation: rules; chain rule; product rule; quotient rule. Higher order derivatives. Implicit differentiation. Taylor series. Optimization problems. Applications to actuarial mathematics: interest rate sensitivity; duration. Partial differentiation. Numerical differentiation. ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Integral Calculus for Act. Sci.
learning_outcomes: apply integration techniques to actuarial problems
evaluate definite and indefinite integrals
apply integral calculus in probability calculations
solve differential equations relevant to actuarial science; and
apply numerical integration methods
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Integration techniques: substitution; integration by parts; partial fractions. Definite integrals. Application to probability distributions. Differential equations: first and second order. Numerical integration: trapezoidal rule; Simpson's rule. Applications to actuarial mathematics. ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Financial Mathematics I
learning_outcomes: understand the time value of money
calculate present and accumulated values
understand different interest rate conventions
price fixed income securities; and
calculate loan repayment schedules
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Simple interest. Compound interest. Force of interest. Effective and nominal rates. Annuities: annuities-due; annuities-immediate; perpetuities; deferred annuities. Loan repayment: level payments; mortgage calculations. Bond pricing: fixed coupon bonds; floating rate bonds; yield to maturity. Duration and convexity. Introduction to term structure of interest rates. ────────────────────────────────

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Financial Mathematics II
learning_outcomes: apply advanced financial mathematics concepts
understand derivative pricing
apply arbitrage-free pricing
understand stochastic interest rate models; and
price interest rate derivatives
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Derivative pricing: forwards; futures; options; swaps. Binomial model for option pricing. Black-Scholes-Merton model. Introduction to stochastic interest rate models. Interest rate derivatives. Credit derivatives. Risk management with derivatives. No-arbitrage pricing. Exotic options. ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Probability Theory II
learning_outcomes: understand multivariate probability distributions
apply the law of total expectation
understand limit theorems
apply generating functions; and
understand stochastic processes basics
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Bivariate distributions: joint; marginal; conditional. Covariance and correlation. Transformations of random variables. Order statistics. Generating functions: probability; moment. Law of total expectation. Convergence of random variables. Law of large numbers. Central limit theorem. Introduction to Markov chains. ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

source_records.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context

describe the global aviation industry structure
identify key stakeholders in the aviation industry
describe the different sectors within the aviation industry; and
explain the basics of flight physics

Aircraft systems overview. Types of aviation: commercial

understand aircraft financing structures

understand airport economics and pricing; and

Airport economics: charges; slot auctions; aeronautical vs. commercial revenues; economic regulation. Capital investment appraisal in aviation. Risk management in aviation finance. IATA economic ou

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Aviation Meteorology
learning_outcomes: understand weather phenomena and their impact on aviation
interpret meteorological reports (METAR, TAF)
identify hazardous weather conditions for flight
understand the impact of weather on aircraft performance; and
describe the role of meteorological services in aviation safety
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Atmosphere structure. Temperature, pressure and density. Clouds and precipitation. Wind and turbulence. Visibility and fog. Icing. Thunderstorms. Tropical meteorology. Weather in Nigeria. Meteorological services for aviation. METAR and TAF interpretation. Wind shear. Impact of weather on aircraft performance and operations. ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

identify airport capacity and demand management

describe airport master planning
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Airport components: runway; taxiway; apron; terminal; airfield lighting. Airport classification: ICAO Annex 14. Airport operations: landing and take-off procedures; ground movement; turnaround. Airport planning: master plan; traffic forecasting; capacity analysis. Terminal operations: passenger processing; baggage handling; check-in. Ground handling services. Airport emergency planning. Environmen

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Airline Operations Management
learning_outcomes: explain how airlines are structured and managed
describe airline network planning
explain fleet management
describe crew management and scheduling; and
explain airline revenue management
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Airline business models: FSC; LCC; charter; regional. Airline network: route planning; hub-and-spoke; point-to-point. Fleet management: selection; financing (ownership; lease). Crew management: rostering; duty time limitations. Revenue management: pricing; yield management; overbooking. Airline cost management. Airline alliances and codesharing. Slot allocation. ───────────────────────────────────

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Aviation Safety and Security
learning_outcomes: explain the regulatory framework for aviation safety
describe the Safety Management System (SMS)
identify common causes of aviation accidents
explain aviation security measures and regulations; and
describe emergency response procedures
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: ICAO safety framework. Safety Management Systems (SMS): hazard identification; risk assessment; safety assurance. Aviation accident investigation: ICAO Annex 13. Human factors in safety: CRM; SHEL model. Aviation security: ICAO Annex 17; threat assessment; screening. Airside security operations. Airport emergency planning. Nigeria's civil aviation safety regulations. ──────────────────────────────

source_records.name: Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context

source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Physics I (Mechanics)
learning_outcomes: identify and deduce the physical quantities and their units
differentiate between vectors and scalars
describe and evaluate motion of systems on the basis of the fundamental laws of mechanics
apply Newton’s laws to describe and solve simple problems of motion
evaluate work, energy, velocity, momentum, acceleration, and torque of moving or rotating objects
explain and apply the principles of conservation of energy, linear and angular momentum
describe the laws governing motion under gravity; and
explain motion under gravity and quantitatively determine behaviour of objects moving under gravity

Kinematics; Newton laws of motion (Inertial frames, Impulse, force and action at a distance, momentum conservation). relative motion. Application of Newtonian mechanics. equations of motion. conservation principles in physics, conservative forces, conservation of linear mo

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Physics II (Electricity & Magnetism)
learning_outcomes: describe the electric field and potential and related concepts, for stationary charges
calculate electrostatic properties of simple charge distributions using Coulomb’s law, Gauss’s law and electric potential
describe and determine the magnetic field for steady and moving charges
determine the magnetic properties of simple current distributions using Biot-Savart and Ampere’s law
describe electromagnetic induction and related concepts and make calculations using Faraday and Lenz’s laws
explain the basic physical of Maxwell’s equations in integral form
evaluate DC circuits to determine the electrical parameters; and
determine the characteristics of AC voltages and currents in resistors, capacitors and inductors
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Forces in nature, electrostatics, electric charge and its properties, methods of charging Coulomb’s law and superposition, electric field and potential, Gauss’s law, capacitance, electric dipoles, energy in electric fields, conductors and insulators, current, voltage and resistance, Ohm’s law and analysis of DC circuits, magnetic fields, Lorentz force, Biot-Savart and Ampère’s laws, magnetic dipol

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Classical Physics I
learning_outcomes: relate the concepts of space coordinates, time and linear motion
describe particle dynamics, equilibrium and conservative forces
solve problems on central forces, energy and angular momentum
explain the dynamics of rotational motion
discuss and apply the potential theory
explain the dynamics of rigid bodies
apply Newton's theory of gravitation to problems of planetary motion and space travel
use inertial forces to explain motion from the viewpoint of rotating frames of reference; and
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Introduction to classical mechanics, space and time, straight line kinematics. Linear and angular momentum, force and torque. Motion in a plane. Newtonian gravity. The two-body systems, forces and equilibrium, particle dynamics, force fields and potentials, collisions, conservative forces, inertial frames and non-inertial frames. Motion in rotating frames. Centrifugal force. Central force motions.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Analytical Mechanics I
learning_outcomes: explain particle motion in one, two, and three dimensions
describe the two body problem and many body systems
define and solve problems of conservative forces
explain Newton theory of gravitation
describe the nature of generalised motion
explain the theory of relativity
identify an appropriate set of generalised coordinates to describe a dynamical system and obtain its Lagrangian in terms of those coordinates and the associated 'velocities'; and
derive and solve the corresponding equations of motion. Treat small oscillations as an eigenvalue problem
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Review of Newtonian Mechanics. Motion of a particle in one, two and three dimensions. Internal forces. External forces. Forces of constraint. Systems of particles and collision theory. Newtonian gravitation; conservative forces and potentials, oscillations, central force problems; accelerated frames of reference. Rigid body dynamics. Rotational problems and space coordinates. Mechanics of continuo

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Electromagnetism
learning_outcomes: explain basic physical laws and concepts in electricity and electromagnetism
use fundamental laws and relation to solve problems in electricity and electromagnetism
explain Maxwell’s equation as a fundamental law of nature integral and the differential form of the equation
give solution for Maxwell’s equation for electrostatic field; and
elucidate the Lorentz’s transformation of the electric and magnetic field
derive Maxwell's equation set from the empirical laws of electromagnetism
apply the fundamental laws of electromagnetism to solve simple problems of electrostatics, magnetostatics and electromagnetic induction in a vacuum
modify Maxwell's laws to apply in the presence of materials and solve problems involving them
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Electrostatics and magnetostatics. Laplace's equation and boundary value problems. Multiple expansions. Dielectric and magnetic materials. Faraday's law. A.C. Circuits. Maxwell's equations. Lorentz’s covariance and special relativity.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Quantum Physics
learning_outcomes: discuss the process leading to the development of quantum physics (origin of quantum physics)
classify and explain the basic difference between classical and quantum physics
explain the purpose and use of mathematical tools of quantum mechanics
solve Schrodinger equation for simple 1D and 3D system; and
apply mathematical and physics skills to solve modern physics problem
explain the origin of quantum physics and principles of quantum theory
apply the mathematical tools of quantum physics
explain how quantum states are described by wave functions
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Wave-particle duality and the uncertainty principle. Basic principles of the quantum theory. Energy levels in potential wells. Reflection and transmission of potential barriers. Atomic and molecular structure. Nuclear reactions. Fission and fusion. Magnetic resonance and elementary particles.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Statistical and Thermal Physics I
learning_outcomes: describe the laws of thermodynamics from both a macroscopic and microscopic point of view
apply the laws of thermodynamics to real physical system and processes
describe the properties of ideal gases using Boltzmann statistics
describe the differences between systems of bosons and fermions and how they arise from microscopic consideration
describe an ideal gas on the basis of classical statistics

illustrate the canonical and grand-canonical partition functions for systems in thermal equilibrium, and use them to obtain thermodynamic quantities of interest
describe the implications of the indistinguishability of particles for systems of non-interacting quantum particles
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Basic concept of statistical mechanics. Microscopic basis of thermodynamics and applications to macroscopic systems. Condensed states. Phase transformations. Quantum distributions. Elementary kinetic theory of transport processes. Fluctuation phenomena and applications.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Quantum Mechanics I
learning_outcomes: demonstrate a clear and structured approach for solving problems
compute the angular momentum of a wave function using operators
describe and compute Eigen functions of the angular momentum operators
explain the relationship between quantum spin and angular momentum; and
apply spin operators to a simple ½ system to perform calculations
state the postulates of quantum mechanics
explain the basics of vectors and tensor operators
solve a variety of physical problems using the Schrodinger equation
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: The formulation of quantum mechanics in terms of state vectors and linear operators. Threedimensional spherically symmetric potentials. The theory of angular momentum and spin. Identical particles and the exclusion principle. Methods of approximation and multielectron atoms.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Digital Electronics
learning_outcomes: explain positive and negative logic states, TTL, MOS, CMOS integrated circuit
illustrate the working of flip-flips; and
develop skills to build and troubleshoot digital electronics circuits

discuss the modern electronic theory of atoms
write electronic configurations of elements on the periodic table
justify the trends of atomic radii, ionization energies, electronegativity of the elements based on their position in the periodic table
identify and balance oxidation – reduction equation and solve redox titration problems
illustrate shapes of simple molecules and hybridized orbitals
identify the characteristics of acids, bases and salts, and solve problems based on their quantitative relationship
apply the principles of equilibrium to aqueous systems using LeChatelier’s principle to predict the effect of concentration, pressure, and temperature changes on equilibrium mixtures
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Atoms, molecules, elements and compounds and chemical reactions. Modern electronic theory of atoms. Electronic configuration, periodicity and building up of the periodic table. Hybridization and shapes of simple molecules. Valence forces and structure of solids. Chemical equations and stoichiometry, chemical bonding and intermolecular forces and kinetic theory of matter. Elementary thermochemistry

learning_outcomes: state the importance and development of organic chemistry
define fullerenes and their applications
discuss electronic theory
determine the qualitative and quantitative of structures in organic chemistry
describe rules guiding nomenclature and functional group classes of organic chemistry
determine rate of reaction to predict mechanisms of reaction
identify classes of organic functional group with brief description of their chemistry
discuss comparative chemistry of group 1A, IIA and IVA elements; and
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Historical survey of the development and importance of Organic Chemistry; Fullerenes as fourth allotrope of carbon, uses as nanotubules, nanostructures, nano chemistry. Electronic theory in organic chemistry. Isolation and purification of organic compounds. Determination of structures of organic compounds including qualitative and quantitative analysis in organic chemistry. Nomenclature and functi

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Chemistry Practical I
learning_outcomes: describe the general laboratory rules and safety procedures
collect scientific data and correctly carrying out Chemical experiments
identify the basic glassware and equipment in the laboratory
differentiate between primary and secondary standards
perform redox titration
record observations and measurements in the laboratory notebooks; and
analyse the data to arrive at scientific conclusions
collect scientific data and correctly carrying out chemical experiment
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Laboratory experiments designed to reflect topics presented in courses CHM 101 and CHM 102. These include acid-base titrations, qualitative analysis, redox reactions, gravimetric analysis, data analysis and presentation.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Chemistry Practical II
learning_outcomes: identify the general laboratory rules and safety procedures
collect scientific data and correctly carrying out chemical experiments
identify the basic glassware and equipment in the laboratory
identify and carry out preliminary tests which includes ignition, boiling point, melting point, test on known and unknown organic compounds
execute solubility tests on known and unknown organic compounds
execute elemental tests on known and unknown compounds; and
conduct functional group/confirmatory test on known and unknown compounds which could be acidic / basic / neutral organic compounds
collect scientific data and correctly carry out chemical experiments
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Continuation of CHM 107. Additional laboratory experiments to include functional group analysis, quantitative analysis using volumetric methods.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Glass –Blowing Technology
learning_outcomes: explain the chemistry of glass, its various types, composition and applications
identify equipment and tools used in the technology of glass-blowing and their associated hazards; and
operate simple glass blowing tools and machines, and carry glass cutting
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: The origin and nature of glass; simple analysis of glass composition. Types of glass commonly used in laboratories. Properties of different glasses commonly used in laboratories. Identification of glass by physical, flame and chemical methods. Design of glassblowing workshop. Identification of various tools and equipment used in the glassblowing workshops. The use of non-return valves and goggles.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Biochemistry I
learning_outcomes: explain the structure of different macromolecules in biological system
identify types of chemical reactions involving these macromolecules
explain the various methods of isolation of these macromolecules
estimate the effects of acids and alkalis on the macromolecules
describe purification of macromolecules; and
discuss quantification of the various macromolecules
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Introductory chemistry of amino acids, their properties, reactions and biological functions. Classification of amino acids: neutral, basic and acidic; polar and non-polar; essential and nonessential amino acids. Peptides. Introductory chemistry and classification of proteins. Biological functions of proteins. Methods of their isolation, purification and identification. Primary, secondary, tertiary

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Biochemistry II
learning_outcomes: explain the structure of the cell including its components
discuss the interrelationship between different organelles of the cell
recognize the differences between plant and animal cells
isolate the various organelles of both plant and animal cells; and
describe the influence of hydrogen ion concentration on cellular function
identify the structure of the cell including its components
explain the influence of hydrogen ion concentration on cellular function

Regulation of water and electrolyte balance. Disorder

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Biochemistry Practical
learning_outcomes: explain classification and chemistry of carbohydrate;
discuss chemistry and biochemistry of the polysaccharide including the amino sugars; mucopolysaccharides, blood group substances;
illustrate structure of chemistry and function of normal living cell;
define metabolism of proteins;
describe carbohydrates, nucleic acids and lipids;
demonstrate basic biochemical importance; and
apply biochemical knowledge in the clinics.
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Laboratory experiments designed to reflect the topics covered in BCH 201 and BCH 202. Introduction to laboratory methods and procedures employed in studying biochemical processes.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Physiology

state the general characteristics of enzymes
describe nutrition, digestion and absorption in plants and animals

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Physical Chemistry I
learning_outcomes: state the kinetic theory of gases and solve problems related to ideal and real gases
derive the formula for molecular velocity of gases and use the derived formula to solve problems
describe and explain the fundamental concepts of physical chemistry including those of statistical mechanics, chemical Kinetics, quantum mechanics and spectroscopy
apply simple models to predict properties of chemical systems

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Organic Chemistry I

describe stereochemistry and its application
describe condition and pathways of the following organic reactions - Grignard reaction, Aldol and related reactions; and
describe simple alicyclic carbon compounds and their synthesis
describe the structures of simple sugars, starch and cellulose, peptides and proteins and show the difference in their conformational structure

source_records.name: Nigerian biomedical, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and epidemiology research context
findings: NIMR describes Nigerian molecular epidemiology, food-safety, immunogenetics, theranostics, microbiome and molecular-technique laboratories; NABDA describes Nigerian biomedical biotechnology work in immunology, vaccinology, antibody generation, DNA, biobanking and diagnostics; NIPRD describes pharmaceutical, biological-product, toxicology, quality-assurance and environmental-science research.
source_records.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

source_records.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_records.name: Nigerian fisheries, aquaculture and aquatic-research context
findings: The Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria identifies a Fisheries and Aquaculture department responsible for coordinating, supervising and regulating research and training, policy, facilities, industry collaboration, sustainable practices and productivity across Nigerian fisheries and aquaculture institutions.
source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian fisheries and aquaculture institutional context, not a vacancy count or one universal qualification, species, production system or equipment stack.

source_records.name: Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context
findings: ARCN coordinates agricultural research, training and extension through national institutes and colleges across Nigeria's agro-ecological zones; its plant-resources work covers crop improvement, seed production, irrigation, pest and disease management, genetics and biotechnology; NIHORT covers fruits, vegetables, spices, ornamentals, post-harvest processing and sustainable horticultural production; NBTE lists Nigerian crop-production and livestock-production technical pathways.
source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

source_records.name: Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operations context
findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_records.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_records.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority radiation-safety training for mining
findings: NNRA announced a 2026 national course for current or prospective Radiation Safety Officers in mining and mineral processing, covering NORM/TE-NORM, monitoring, dose assessment, radiation protection, handling, transport, waste management and regulatory compliance.
source_records.limitations: This is a specialised radiation-safety pathway and does not apply to every mining or geology role.

source_records.name: Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_records.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Physics I
learning_outcomes: identify and deduce the physical quantities and their units
differentiate between vectors and scalars
describe and evaluate motion of systems on the basis of the fundamental laws of mechanics
apply Newton’s laws to describe and solve simple problems of motion
evaluate work, energy, velocity, momentum, acceleration, and torque of moving or rotating objects
explain and apply the principles of conservation of energy, linear and angular momentum
describe the laws governing motion under gravity; and
explain motion under gravity and quantitatively determine behaviour of objects moving under gravity
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Space and time. Units and dimension, vectors and scalars, differentiation of vectors: displacement, velocity and acceleration. Kinematics; Newton laws of motion (Inertial frames, Impulse, force and action at a distance, momentum conservation). relative motion. Application of Newtonian mechanics. equations of motion. conservation principles in physics, conservative forces, conservation of linear mo

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Physics V (Elementary Modern Physics)
learning_outcomes: identify the circumstances, discoveries and people that launched modern physics
enumerate and understand the postulate of relativity
explain the problem of simultaneity and calculate time changes from one frame of reference to another
describe relativistic length contraction
describe the relativistic mass-energy relation
explain the work of Planck, Bohr and Heisenberg; and
explain the uncertainty principle and the other features of Quantum mechanics
explain the notion of an inertial frame and the concept of an observer
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Special relativity. Defects in Newtonian mechanics. The speed of light. The Lorentz transformation. Transformation of velocities. Experimental basis of quantum theory. Black body radiation. Electrons and quanta. Bohr's theory of atomic structure. De-Broglie hypothesis. The uncertainty principle. Schrodinger's equation and simple applications.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Introduction to Electric Circuits and Electronics
learning_outcomes: identify circuit diagrams and symbols
determine current flows, potential drops, power, and energy dissipation in circuits using Ohm’s law
simplify series and parallel combinations of resistors
state Kirchhoff’s laws and apply same in solving for currents and voltages in D.C. and A.C. circuits
apply potential divider and current divider techniques in calculating circuit potential differences and branch currents
state and apply circuit theorems and principles to solve problems
apply the Mesh currents and Node – Voltage methods in network analysis
discuss the nature of ac. currents and voltages in resistors, inductors, capacitors and determine impedances
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: D.C. Circuits. Sources of emf and current. Resistor combinations. Kirchhoff’s Laws. Network analysis and circuit theorems. Mesh currents method, Node-voltage, Thevenin and Norton theorem, superposition principle. A.C. Circuits. Sinusoidal wave-forms. RMS and peak values. Power. Resistance, inductance and capacitance in a.c. circuits. Impedance and admittance. Series and parallel RLC circuits. Q fa

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Physics IV (Waves and Optics)
learning_outcomes: explain the purpose and use of mathematical tools relating to waves and optics
account the difference between wave equation of motion and the Newtonian mechanics
discuss the working principle of optical system; and
design optical instruments
describe the wave phenomena and explain the nature and properties of waves
explain wave propagation in different media
describe geometric optics and image formation
analyse simple examples of interference and diffraction phenomena
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Wave phenomena; Acoustical waves; the harmonic oscillator; waves on a string; energy in wave motion; longitudinal waves; standing waves; group and phase velocity; Doppler effect; Physical Optics; Spherical waves; interference and diffraction, thin films; crystal diffraction, holography; dispersion and scattering. Geometrical Optics; Waves and rays; reflection at a spherical surface, thin lenses, o

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Electromagnetism I
learning_outcomes: explain basic physical laws and concepts in electricity and electromagnetism
use fundamental laws and relation to solve problems in electricity and electromagnetism
explain Maxwell’s equation as a fundamental law of nature integral and the differential form of the equation
give solution for Maxwell’s equation for electrostatic field; and
elucidate the Lorentz’s transformation of the electric and magnetic field
derive Maxwell's equation set from the empirical laws of electromagnetism
apply the fundamental laws of electromagnetism to solve simple problems of electrostatics, magnetostatics and electromagnetic induction in a vacuum
modify Maxwell's laws to apply in the presence of materials and solve problems involving them
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Electrostatics and magnetostatics. Laplace's equation and boundary value problems. Multiple expansions. Dielectric and magnetic materials. Faraday's law. A.C. Circuits. Maxwell's equations. Lorentz’s covariance and special relativity.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Quantum Physics
learning_outcomes: discuss the process leading to the development of quantum physics (origin of quantum physics)
classify and explain the basic difference between classical and quantum physics
explain the purpose and use of mathematical tools of quantum mechanics
solve Schrodinger equation for simple 1D and 3D system; and
apply mathematical and physics skills to solve modern physics problem
explain the origin of quantum physics and principles of quantum theory
apply the mathematical tools of quantum physics
explain how quantum states are described by wave functions
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Wave-particle duality and the uncertainty principle. Basic principles of the quantum theory. Energy levels in potential wells. Reflection and transmission of potential barriers. Atomic and molecular structure. Nuclear reactions. Fission and fusion. Magnetic resonance and elementary particles.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Statistical and Thermal Physics
learning_outcomes: describe the laws of thermodynamics from both a macroscopic and microscopic point of view
apply the laws of thermodynamics to real physical system and processes
describe the properties of ideal gases using Boltzmann statistics
describe the differences between systems of bosons and fermions and how they arise from microscopic consideration
describe an ideal gas on the basis of classical statistics
explain the basic concepts of statistical mechanics, including entropy, its statistical interpretation and relation to disorder, and the statistical origin of the second law of thermodynamics
illustrate the canonical and grand-canonical partition functions for systems in thermal equilibrium, and use them to obtain thermodynamic quantities of interest
describe the implications of the indistinguishability of particles for systems of non-interacting quantum particles
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Basic concept of statistical mechanics. Microscopic basis of thermodynamics and applications to macroscopic systems. Condensed states. Phase transformations. Quantum distributions. Elementary kinetic theory of transport processes. Fluctuation phenomena and applications.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Electronics
learning_outcomes: describe behaviours of semiconductors and their significance in the development of modern electronics
explain the operation of semiconductor devices and their advantages over their vacuum tube counter parts; and
demonstrate the significance of modulation in telecommunication
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Thermionic emission, vacuum tubes: diodes and transistors; semiconductors; p-n junction; characteristics of p-n junction; uses of diodes; bipolar junction and unipolar transistors, transistor biasing, transistor switch. Equivalent circuits of semi-conductors, diodes, transistors. Small and large signal operations. Wave from generation by transistors. Class A, B. and C amplifiers. Feedback amplifie

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
learning_outcomes: demonstrate a clear and structured approach for solving problems
compute the angular momentum of a wave function using operators
describe and compute Eigen functions of the angular momentum operators
explain the relationship between quantum spin and angular momentum; and
apply spin operators to a simple ½ system to perform calculations
state the postulates of quantum mechanics
explain the basics of vectors and tensor operators
solve a variety of physical problems using the Schrodinger equation
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: The formulation of quantum mechanics in terms of state vectors and linear operators. Threedimensional spherically symmetric potentials. The theory of angular momentum and spin. Identical particles and the exclusion principle. Methods of approximation and multielectron atoms.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Solid State Physics II
learning_outcomes: apply electrical exploration method
demonstrate and apply principles of borehole drilling
operate X-ray machines for medical diagnosis
describe operations and maintenance of MRI machines
design and analyse analogue and digital electronics systems; and
apply techniques of troubleshooting in analogue and digital electronics systems
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Electrical resistivity exploration method, principles of borehole geophysics, methods of medical Xray radiography, techniques of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), design and analysis of analogue electronics systems, design and analysis of digital electronics systems, methods of troubleshooting in analogue and digital systems, methods of troubleshooting in digital computers.

source_records.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context

source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_records.name: Nigerian fisheries, aquaculture and aquatic-research context

source_records.name: Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context

Nigerian university curricula describe anatomy, physiology, therapeutic exercise and patient-care preparation for rehabilitation practice.
source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian profession and education context; exact registration, scope and supervision depend on the profession and current regulator, and it does not establish a vacancy count for every therapy title.

source_records.name: Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_records.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_records.name: Nigerian lifestyle medicine, rehabilitation, fitness and wellness context

source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian wellness and lifestyle-medicine context; it does not establish one licence or clinical scope for every coach, trainer, therapist, dietitian or recreational role.

learning_outcomes: explain the basic physical processes underpinning Radiography
apply physical principles in understanding and practice of diagnostic medical imaging devices and procedures;
identify the sources of radiation and mechanisms of their production for both ionizing and non- ionizing;
describe its physical characteristics and interaction with matter especially biological systems and
explain the application of radiation in medicine, biology and industry Allied Health Sciences               713                                       New
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Fundamental and derived quantities and units. Equation of motion, concepts of force work energy, power, momentum energy conservation. Fields, Electrostatics, Physical Factors governing capacitance, charging and discharging capacitor and their uses in Radiological Equipment, basic x-ray circuitry and many others. Basic computer Architecture and peripherals. Electromagnetic and Electromagnetic induc

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Radiobiology, Radiation Dosimetry and Protection
learning_outcomes: demonstrate clarity in communicating the biological basis of radiation protection
describe international standards and practices for safety in all applications of radiation for medicine and industry. Students should carry out measurements using radiation dosimetry equipment;
describe principles of operation of radiation dosemeters; and
apply principle of radiation protection in radiology and other settings
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Cell theory and genetic apparatus, radiation chemistry, effect of radiation on DNA molecules, amino acid, protein and many others, cellular damages, survival curves. Theories of Biological effects of radiation, short and long term effect (stochastic and non-stochastic, radio sensitivity and Modifiers, post irradiation clinic events, organ pathology syndromes, evidence from Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Radiographic Anatomy and Physiology I
learning_outcomes: relate the anatomy of the various parts of the body learnt with the appearances on radiographs for both plain and contrast studies;
identify and differentiate appearances in different modalities eg u/s MRI and many others
recognise normal, pathological, morphological and functional changes on radiographs caused by disease entities covering major organs and systems of the body; and
explain the basis for additional projections during imaging
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Conventional and contrast Radiographic Anatomy of the system. Anatomy applied to ultrasound and nuclear medicine. Surface anatomy and cross- sectional anatomy. Identification and recognition of normal and pathological changes in anatomical structures and physiological processes. Basic manifestations and presentations of various pathological conditions and diseases entities on radiographs, ultrasou

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Radio-Nuclide Imaging /Thermography/MRI
learning_outcomes: determine the type of nuclide, radio pharmaceuticals and quality tests for various radio- nuclide imaging procedures and calculate administered dose;
describe the safety precautions, standard procedures and disposal of radioactive wastes are the expected outcome;
recognise the need for special consideration in siting the MRI Unit
describe the principles and mechanisms of its operations and be familiar with technologies associated with MRI;
describe the protocols that obtain best images for various pathologies and body parts
apply safety precautions involved in MRI procedures; and
describe methods of artefact reduction
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Basic principles, Decay schemes of Radionuclide production, cyclotron design and performance, radiopharmaceuticals, impurity levels. Equipment for nuclear medicine generators, procedures, contamination monitoring. Radioisotope image, gamma camera electronics, uniformity correction, dead time performance factors � collimators, shielding requirements, internal dosimetry. Disposal of radioactive wast

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Rural Radiography
learning_outcomes: recognise the role of radiographers at primary healthcare level level, particularly the use of x- rays and ultrasound to provide diagnostic information in pediatric emergencies, perinatal and other medical/surgical emergencies;
explain the principles and methods of public health education and administration and the social responsibilities of healthcare personnel in communicable and non-communicable diseases environment;
integrate principles of preventive medicine in diagnostic medical imaging; and
describe the role of a radiographer as an effective team member in delivery of health service in the rural area.

identify important forest tree species as well as wildlife species in the various vegetation zones of Nigeria

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: A survey of New World Archaeology
learning_outcomes: identify the different stages of archaeological development in the new world and characterise each;
articulate the evidence for food production in the new world and argue in what ways, it differs from similar evidence in the old world;
identify and characterise the major civilizations of the new world and argue how and why they collapsed; and
understand the extent to which the environment played a major role in the rise and collapse of civilizations in the new word.

Energy capture in the New world.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Archaeology of Africa
learning_outcomes: clearly argue out how africa is the cradle of humankind
analyse how agriculture and metallurgy led to the development of complex societies in africa;
identify the significance of the nile valley, east and southern africa in the archaeology of the continent; and
explain the bantu problematic and the different lines of inquiry used in bantu studies
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: The African paleo environment. Language families in Africa. Africa and human origins. Stone Age cultures of Africa. Food production in Africa. Egypt and the Nile valley. The African Iron Age and Bantu migrations.

learning_outcomes: list the characteristics, methods of identification and classification of viruses, bacteria and fungi
state the unique characteristics of plant and animal kingdoms
describe ecological adaptations in the plant and animal kingdoms
explain nutrition, respiration, excretion and reproduction in plants and animals; and
describe growth and development in plants and animals
List the characteristics, methods of identification and classification of viruses, bacteria and fungi
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Basic characteristics, identification and classification of viruses, bacteria and fungi. A generalized survey of the plant and animal kingdoms based mainly on the study of similarities and differences in the external features. Ecological adaptations. Briefs on physiology to include nutrition, respiration, circulatory systems, excretion, reproduction, growth and development.

Biological drawings and illustration, scaling, accuracy and proportion. use of common laboratory apparatus and laboratory experiments designed to illustrate the topics covered in BIO 101.

Types of fruits and seeds. Care and use of dissecting kits and other biological wares. Dissection and general histology of animal tissues based on vertebrate forms. explain the thermal stratification of lakes
summarize the importance and interplay of oxygen, carbon-dioxide and pH in water,
describe fresh water communities

The chemical composition of African

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Biostatistics
learning_outcomes: differentiate between continuous and discontinuous data
explain sampling procedures in biology
summarize and present biological data
describe measures of central tendency and probability theory; and
conduct ANOVA, Chi-square, t-tests and F-tests and state their importance
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Variability in biological data: continuous and discontinuous variables. Statistical sampling procedures. Observations and problems of estimation. Representation and summarization of biological data. Frequency distribution. Measures of central tendency and dispersion. Probability theory. Normal, binomial and Poisson distribution. T-test, f-test and chi-square test. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) and

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Population Biology and Evolution
learning_outcomes: explain the concept of natural selection
summarize evolution of some organisms
discuss how organisms adapt to their environment
apply mathematical formulae and models to genetic variations and predictions in population; and
describe factors responsible for population changes
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Biological properties of species. Natural selection. Variations, isolation mechanisms (including their breakdown resulting in hybridization, adaptation, origin of life, origin of species and adaptive radiation, evolution of selected groups of plants and animals, including humans). Population dynamics. Factors affecting population growth.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Biogeography and Soil Biology

outline the world key flora and fauna groups and reasons for their distribution
explain succession, colonisation and dispersal of plants and animals
describe the concept of endemicity, refugia and Island biogeography
discuss physical and chemical nature of soil
summarise the cycling of minerals and nutrients
explain soil and animal soil water relationship; and

nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Gondwanaland and theory of continental drift. Theory of land bridges. Distribution of world key floral and faunal groups including factors affecting distribution. Phyto- and zoogeographyical regions of the world. Relationships between plants and animal distributions (emphasising local examples). Concept of succession, colonisation and dispersal in terrestrial plants and animals. Concept of endemic

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Systemic Biology
learning_outcomes: describe the pre-Linnaean, Linnaean and Darwinian taxonomic concepts of species
explain the binomial system of nomenclature
classify organisms based on the binomial system of nomenclature; and
explain the concept of keys and keying and their applications
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Historical background, pre-Linnaean, Linnaean and Darwinian taxonomic hierarchies. Species concept, categories below species and categories above species. Biological nomenclature, new systematics; numerical and binomial taxonomy. Keys and keying.

source_records.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

source_records.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_records.name: Nigerian fisheries, aquaculture and aquatic-research context

source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian fisheries and aquaculture institutional context, not a vacancy count or one universal qualification, species, production system or equipment stack.

source_records.name: Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context
findings: ARCN coordinates agricultural research, training and extension through national institutes and colleges across Nigeria's agro-ecological zones; its plant-resources work covers crop improvement, seed production, irrigation, pest and disease management, genetics and biotechnology; NIHORT covers fruits, vegetables, spices, ornamentals, post-harvest processing and sustainable horticultural production; NBTE lists Nigerian crop-production and livestock-production technical pathways.
source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

source_records.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.

source_records.name: Nigerian fisheries, aquaculture and aquatic-research context

source_records.name: Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: General Chemistry I
learning_outcomes: define atom, molecules, and chemical reactions
discuss the modern electronic theory of atoms
write electronic configurations of elements on the periodic table
justify the trends of atomic radii, ionization energies, electronegativity of the elements based on their position in the periodic table
identify and balance oxidation – reduction equation and solve redox titration problems
illustrate shapes of simple molecules and hybridized orbitals
identify the characteristics of acids, bases and salts, and solve problems based on their quantitative relationship
apply the principles of equilibrium to aqueous systems using LeChatelier’s principle to predict the effect of concentration, pressure, and temperature changes on equilibrium mixtures
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Atoms, molecules, elements and compounds and chemical reactions. Modern electronic theory of atoms. Electronic configuration, periodicity and building up of the periodic table. Hybridization and shapes of simple molecules. Valence forces and structure of solids. Chemical equations and stoichiometry, chemical bonding and intermolecular forces and kinetic theory of matter. Elementary thermochemistry

source_records.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_records.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_records.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_records.name: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing and metal-production training context
findings: NBTE publishes Nigerian national curricula and occupational standards for fabrication and welding, fitting, welding and fabrication, blacksmithing and foundry, and related technical pathways; the standards include safety, statutory compliance, marking out, welding, fastening, bending, thermal cutting, sawing and abrasive cutting.
source_records.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

source_records.name: Nigerian industrial automation, robotics and mechatronics training context
findings: NBTE curricula identify Nigerian training in automation and robotics, including relays, switches, contactors, machine programming, automated production lines, numerical control, automated assembly, PLC programming and fault diagnosis, robotics, mechatronics and human-machine interfaces.
source_records.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

learning_outcomes: list the characteristics, methods of identification and classification of viruses, bacteria and fungi
state the unique characteristics of plant and animal kingdoms
describe ecological adaptations in the plant and animal kingdoms
explain nutrition, respiration, excretion and reproduction in plants and animals; and
describe growth and development in plants and animals
List the characteristics, methods of identification and classification of viruses, bacteria and fungi
nigerian_curriculum_courses.content_summary: Basic characteristics, identification and classification of viruses, bacteria and fungi. A generalized survey of the plant and animal kingdoms based mainly on the study of similarities and differences in the external features. Ecological adaptations. Briefs on physiology to include nutrition, respiration, circulatory systems, excretion, reproduction, growth and development.

nigerian_curriculum_courses.title: Population Biology and Evolution
learning_outcomes: explain the concept of natural selection
summarize evolution of some organisms

source_records.name: Nigerian state and local-government office context

source_records.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.
